name: LFM3-Audio-2B

lineage.base_model: LFM3 backbone with an in-house causal audio encoder and the LiquidCodec tokenizer; successor of LFM2.5-Audio (card)

purpose: Compact, fully featured audio model that runs locally on laptops and edge devices: text or audio in, text, speech or both out. Voice chat, multilingual transcription, speech synthesis and translation, audio understanding, tool calling from spoken requests (card).

license.name: LFM Open License v1.0
license.notes: LICENSE read: Apache-2.0-style grant (copyright license, redistribution, derivative works) with a Commercial Use Limitation in section 5: commercial use is licensed only for Legal Entities whose annual revenue is below USD 10,000,000 (the Threshold, counted across controlled and controlling entities); above it a separate agreement is needed. Qualified non-profits are exempt for non-commercial or research use. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: LFM3 backbone with causal audio encoder (sliding-window attention plus short convolutions) and LiquidCodec audio tokenizer (12 discrete tokens per 80 ms of speech, streaming decoding)
architecture.why_this_design: Card: the causal encoder uses sliding-window attention and short convolutions to keep memory bounded and supports live audio and incremental prefill; LiquidCodec powers multilingual speech generation and supports streaming decoding.

variants.notes: Q8_0 1.85 GB, BF16 3.47 GB; mmproj Q8_0 0.3 GB; 270k downloads on the HF API

engine_support.notes: Card lists GGUF for llama.cpp and ONNX for ONNX Runtime.

benchmarks.name: English ASR average WER (ESB / Open ASR suite) and multilingual FLEURS mean error rate over 9 languages incl. German
benchmarks.harness: card compares LFM2.5-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni and Voxtral Mini; numeric cells were not read reliably from the HTML tables

strengths: One 2B model for ASR, TTS, translation and tool calling
Live ASR in 0.96 s chunks (English only)
weaknesses: Voice chat is English only; LiveASR English only
Card says it is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning
License limits commercial use above USD 10M revenue
best_for: on-device voice agents with tool calls
soft.maturity: Liquid AI LFM family; 17k downloads (safetensors) and 270k (GGUF) on the HF API.

tona_fit.reason: Interesting as a single small model for dictation plus TTS plus voice tool calls, but dedicated ASR (parakeet class) and TTS models are likely better per task; German numbers missing. Hybrid LFM backbone is a new architecture for Tona.
blockers: LFM3 backbone, audio encoder and LiquidCodec not in Tona
numeric German ASR/TTS quality not read

open_questions: Numeric English and multilingual ASR results (tables in card)
Exact backbone layout of LFM3 (card refers to blog)
